displayed_attributes.title: 501c3 Lawyer?
displayed_attributes.body:
We have someone that wants to donate millions of dollars to a nonprofit fund that we are trying to make exist as quickly as possible.

How can we do that as quickly as humanly possible?

top_comment.body:
I'm a lawyer that has set up multiple non-profits for multiple purposes. I also ran a 501c3 that had a 501c4 sister organization and a for-profit C-Corp subsidiary.  

Given the amount of money that will be going in, the nonprofit fund will not qualify for obtaining exemption using the 1023-ez path. The nonprofit fund will have to apply using a full 1023 application, which could take around 3-6 months to receive approval. Here is the timeline you should expect:

1. One week to set up the nonprofit organization as an entity (nonstock, nonprofit DE corporation will be fine for this). 

2. One to two weeks to complete the 1023, if you expedite and devote a reasonable amount of time to the process. 

3. Once the 1023 is created, it will take roughly 3-6 months to obtain exemption. If you fill out a clean application that is a slam dunk and doesn't require responses to IRS inquiries, the timeline will be on the shorter end. To create a clean application, you will want to clearly articulate why the organization qualifies as a non-profit, as well its charitable function.

4. If the organization obtains exemption, the exempt status applies back to the date of nonprofit formation (so long as application for exemption occurs within 27 months of formation). In other words, if the entity is formed and operated as a nonprofit even without obtaining official exemption, those activities before obtaining exempt status will be covered as exempt upon being granted exemption. Of course, there is the risk that the application does not go through. 

5. Please be aware that the organization will also need to register the organization in each state that the organization has operations. Additionally, the organization will have to likely apply for exempt status in each such state, as well as apply to solicit charitable donations in each such state. Some localities also offer tax exempt certificates for certain costs and fees paid/incurred.

Nonprofit Pro Tip: Be aware the depending on the type of organization, you may need to meet certain public support standards (minimum donation requirements), which can be thrown off by very large donations that are disproportionate to the size of regularly received donations. As a note, sometimes large donations can be exempted from a public support analysis if the donation meets certain standards.

displayed_attributes.title: Ask Bookface: Stripe Atlas equivalent for 501c3 non profit? other non-profit advice?
displayed_attributes.body:
Hey Bookface,

Does anyone have any pointers on where to start? Swyftflilings, Legal Zoom - good options? Does the state you register the non-profit matter?

Context: Our family is looking to start a non-profit to help future patients that suffer from ALS.

Our father was diagnosed with ALS 3 years ago and recently passed away on August 20th, 2022. He battled this disease until his very last breath. Recently, we were close to securing therapies that could have made a real difference for him. We planned to raise money to help pay for the medication, but his disease progressed too quickly in his final weeks (bookface post [here](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/posts/64917)). We launched a [GoFundMe](https://www.gofundme.com/f/battlewithben), and had a donor offer to put in $25K, but we need to first get 501c3 status. 

Any feedback or advice is appreciated. Thanks!

top_comment.body: First I want this same thing. But second, have you considered partnering with existing non profits with whom you share values and mission? There is a certain amount of overhead creating a non profit that may or may not be worth it to you. Best of luck.

displayed_attributes.title: Investing through a DAF or 501c3?
displayed_attributes.body:
Hi everyone. Hoping to tap into this group's knowledge. My family has always been committed to giving towards 'traditional' charities (poverty, hunger, development initiatives). Being in the tech and YC community though, I've been wondering if we can make our $ go farther by taking high risk bets in impactful startups (whether non profits or not). 

Is there a model for this type of angel investing by means of a non-profit vehicle? Are there any good examples of orgs doing this well? We want to do this through a DAF or 501c3 so that the money we invest is tax deductible, but any gains would go right back to the fund. The goal is to make bets on impactful companies and have that fund be sustaining. 

Thanks!

top_comment.body: You should talk to Founders Pledge. They are extremely familiar with tax optimization stuff around donations, and would likely know the answer or know who to talk to! Let me know if you need an intro.
